name: Modern SEO M2 L3: Citations and Trust Signals that Work
body:
> Module 2, 8:44 (speech ends at about 6:20; the rest is a silent, frozen screen). Source: Lesson 3 Citations and Trust Signals that Work.mp4

## In short
- Step 3 of the low competition ranking method: get verified citations on platforms Google trusts, not random directory submissions "as if it were 2017."
- The instructor uses LeadSnap, but says any tool is fine.
- Connect the GBP to LeadSnap, sync the business details from the GBP, fill every field, then turn on the citation subscription ($20 per month per location).
- Read the citation statuses correctly: many "Submitted" and "Updating" listings will never show "Live" even though they are fine, and "Action required" often needs no action.
- LeadSnap is also used to keep the GBP active: geotagged photos dripped weekly, services, AI-written posts scheduled weekly, Q&A and review responses.

## Key ideas
- **Verified citations, not directories.** The goal is verified business profiles on platforms that require proof the business is legitimate. (0:02)
- **Tool choice is open.** "If you don't want to use the lead snap tool, no problem." (0:02 to 0:34)
- **Manage the GBP from LeadSnap where possible.** After the Lesson 1 and 2 audits, he makes most GBP changes through LeadSnap. Exception: LeadSnap cannot change categories, so those are done in the GBP itself. (1:08 to 1:43)
- **Photos.** Ask the client for photos and upload them. LeadSnap can geotag them and drip them out one photo per week. (1:43)
- **Posts.** Write posts yourself or have AI write them from a prompt, choose a tone, choose emojis or hashtags, and schedule once a week. (2:14)
- **Citation business details.** Use "Sync values from GBP profile," then fill in what is missing: email, keywords, short description, social links (from the website), payment options (from the Lesson 1 questionnaire). Every box should be filled, both in the GBP and in LeadSnap. (2:49 to 3:22)
- **Turn on the subscription only after client approval** and after the GBP changes are made. (3:54)
- **Status meanings** (3:54 to 5:32):
  - **Live:** the publisher has a two-way API connection and confirmed back to LeadSnap.
  - **Submitted:** data was sent but the publisher has no two-way API, so it will always stay "Submitted." Most are actually fine.
  - **Updating:** LeadSnap keeps sending new data. Will almost never show "Live."
  - **Action required:** says it needs claiming, but usually clicking through shows an active citation with nothing to do.

## Step-by-step process
1. In LeadSnap, go to GBP, Manage Locations, and add the location by choosing the Google account that has manager access to the GBP. (0:34)
2. Click Activate on the location so it becomes part of LeadSnap. (1:08)
3. Make the approved GBP changes from Lessons 1 and 2 through LeadSnap where allowed. Change categories in the GBP itself. (1:08 to 1:43)
4. Upload client photos and set them to geotag and drip one per week. (1:43)
5. Add services. (2:14)
6. Create posts (your own or AI written), set tone and options, and schedule them weekly. (2:14)
7. Go to Citations, then Business Details, and click "Sync values from GBP profile." (2:49)
8. Check service areas, categories and services pulled through. Add email, keywords, a short description, social media links and payment options. (2:49 to 3:22)
9. Get client permission and finish the GBP backend changes before going further. (3:54)
10. Tick the subscription box ($20 per month per location) and click Continue. (3:22 to 3:54)
11. After some time, review the listings dashboard: Live, Submitted, Updating, Action required. (3:54)
12. For any "Action required" item, click through to view the citation and check whether anything really needs claiming. (5:01)

## Checklist
- GBP connected to LeadSnap (or your chosen citation tool) and activated
- Approved GBP changes made (categories done directly in the GBP)
- Photos uploaded and set to drip weekly
- Services added
- Weekly posts scheduled
- Citation business details synced from the GBP
- Email, keywords, short description, social links and payment options filled in
- Every field filled in both the GBP and the citation tool
- Client permission received before turning on the subscription
- Citation subscription turned on
- Listing statuses reviewed after some time
- "Action required" items clicked through and checked

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| LeadSnap, Manage Locations | Connecting and activating the GBP | 0:34 |
| LeadSnap GBP management (Photos, Services, Posts, Q&A, Reviews) | Keeping the GBP updated and active | 1:43 to 2:49 |
| LeadSnap Citations, Business Details | Syncing GBP data and filling citation fields | 2:49 |
| LeadSnap citation subscription | Pushing the listing to citation platforms, $20 per month per location | 3:22 |
| LeadSnap Listings dashboard | Showing Live, Submitted, Updating and Action required counts | 3:54 |
| Client questionnaire (from Lesson 1) | Source for payment options and other fields | 3:22 |

Platforms visible on the listings screen (5:25 frame): Google Assistant and Alexa (voice search), Instagram, Foursquare and Nextdoor (social), Google Maps, Waze, Nokia Here, TomTom, Navmii, Uber and Where To (mobile and navigation).

## Numbers and benchmarks
- Verified listings across 51 platforms "without manual verification." (0:02)
- LeadSnap citations cost $20 per month per location. (3:22)
- Photos drip out one per week; posts scheduled once a week. (1:43, 2:14)
- Example dashboard: 47 listings, 15 live, 18 submitted. On screen also 12 updating and 1 action required. (3:54)
- On screen only: LeadSnap notes "most directories accept a maximum of 100 services." (3:45 frame)

## Terms
**Citation:** A listing of the business (name, address, phone and details) on another platform.
**Super citation:** The instructor's term for a verified business profile on a trusted platform, as opposed to a regular directory submission.
**Two-way API connection:** The platform receives LeadSnap's data and sends back a confirmation, which is what shows the listing as "Live."
**Geotagging:** Adding location data to photos before they are uploaded.
**Drip:** Releasing photos or posts on a schedule instead of all at once.

## Worth quoting
- "This isn't about submitting to random directories as if it were 2017." (0:02)
- "These submitted ones will never go to live." (4:29)
- "It doesn't actually need to be claimed." (5:01)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Decide on the tool with Kim first.** LeadSnap costs $20 per month per location, and Kim's rule is no paid services without her approval (memory file `feedback_no_paid_services.md`). Module 1 Lesson 5 says citations can also be done manually for free. Present both options for Pipeliners, Alphalete and Summit AZ.
- **Use the field list as a NAP and details check.** Whatever tool is used, make sure the citation data matches each GBP: name, address, phone, website, email, hours, services, social links and payment options.
- **Summit AZ phone:** citations should carry the real number (480) 447-7008, not a DNI pool number (memory file `feedback_summit_ghl_dni.md`).
- **Keep the GBP active.** Recommend a weekly photo and post rhythm per client. Photos must follow the TAG rule from Scott's meetings: internal pipe damage or lining work only, never under-sink plumbing (memory file `project_tag_meeting_decisions.md`). For Pipeliners posts, check whether Scott's wording rules for blogs should also apply (memory file `feedback_scott_pipeliners_blog_prefs.md`). Confirm with Kim.
- **Read status reports calmly.** If a citation tool shows many "Submitted" or "Action required" items, click through before assuming something is broken.
- **Approval first.** Same as the lesson: no subscription or GBP change goes live until it is approved.

## Open questions
- The intro promises to show "how these super citations differ from regular directory submissions," but the lesson does not really explain it. The explanation is in Module 1 Lesson 5 (verification on platforms like Apple Maps and Bing Places).
- 51 platforms (intro) vs 47 listings on the example dashboard. Unclear in video whether the dashboard is for this client or another one, or why the counts differ.
- Dashboard counts on screen (15 + 18 + 12 + 1 = 46) do not add up to 47; one listing (Instagram) shows no status.
- "Without manual verification" and the trust value of these platforms are instructor claims, not verified.
- The $20 price is as stated in the video and may have changed.
- The video runs from about 6:20 to 8:40 with no speech and a frozen screen, then a fragment of the intro repeats at 8:40.
- No low-confidence lines in the manifest.

## Timestamps
- 0:02 Intro: step 3, verified citations
- 0:34 Any tool is fine; adding a location in LeadSnap
- 1:08 Activating the GBP, making changes through LeadSnap
- 1:43 LeadSnap can't change categories; photos geotagged and dripped weekly
- 2:14 Services and AI posts scheduled weekly
- 2:49 Citations, Business Details, sync from GBP
- 3:22 Filling in remaining fields, $20 per month subscription
- 3:54 Wait for client permission; example dashboard
- 4:29 Two-way API, Submitted vs Live, Updating
- 5:01 Action required and claiming
- 5:32 Wrap-up: citations plus ongoing GBP management
